chapter: La Cigalle and settling in Paris
title: Why he avoids leading a band
summary: Waters liked six days' steady work and has refused leadership because of musicians' drinking and fights. He now works as a soloist with local rhythm sections.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So while you're at the Cigalle the first time with Jacques Butler, that's, you became involved with somebody in that and you more or less started anchoring yourself a little bit more in Europe, but you still were thinkin' of coming back.
Yeah, because I, we worked six days a week, I think we was that way, six days a week.
Steady work has always been very important to you because Charlie Miller had more steady work in Philly and everything -

Yeah, that was, I had the idea of a leader, you know, you gotta be - that's kind of stupid 'cause you - you know, I've refused leadership, that's a bad point. I didn't want to bother with musicians, everybody drunk and then fightin' and all that kind of stuff, you know what I mean to say? I figured I'd be upset if I played with somebody else, I can take care of my own business, you know, like I used to feel that way. That's why I didn't get out as much maybe as I should have. Now I'm interested in whether or not - I'm still not interested in leader [sic] a band, you know? The only way I'm [a] leader in a band is to have an agent that will secure, give me security of so many jobs a week, like a guarantee. Or a job like your job, you say, like musicians stay on your job for a year or somethin' like that, which they don't - but I'm saying something like that. Then I would like to form a band, 'cause I can do my best when I have my own band, everybody can. See, but other than that I prefer to work at - now I'm working as a soloist. It's hard, because I work ten concerts a year and work with, sometimes - on [ ] I went to England the first time, I did twenty days. Out of the twenty days I only worked four days with the same band. Four days, that's it - out of the sixteen days I worked with "deh deh", "deh deh", "deh deh", "deh deh" -

And I caught hell. 'Cause I had explained this, "I don't have time, the guys can't rehearse" and some of 'em were amateurs - this guy lived in Manchester, the other guy lives in so-and-so, the other guy (laughs) lives, and they're working, some of them, you know. But the - now I'm established, I work with the same group so often that they know what I'm doing, you know?
But at first I caught hell.
